gen-silkscreen-gf-tasa-explorer: Curves that stop like brush strokes lifted early give this plain sans a friendly, clean read. TASA Explorer sits under Silkscreen's flat, spaced-out lettering and softens its lo-fi, retro edge.
gen-silkscreen-gf-tasa-orbiter: Space you can almost feel surrounds every letter in Silkscreen, a lo-fi, retro display face. But TASA Orbiter keeps every small counter unclogged, a clean, professional sans-serif body that holds the pair together.
gen-silkscreen-gf-teachers: Thin steel rod bent into letters, with ink strokes that taper out before touching, gives this plain sans a modern look. Teachers stays light beneath Silkscreen, the lo-fi, retro display heading.
gen-silkscreen-gf-telex: Silkscreen gives the heading a lo-fi, retro look, with space around every letter you can almost feel. But paragraphs of Telex come out clean, its curvy letters feeling unclamped on the page.
gen-silkscreen-gf-tenor-sans: Silkscreen draws its g in one unchanging line weight. Tenor Sans, a sans-serif with c tips that never creep toward touching, can be set a touch larger to show its light stroke variation.
gen-silkscreen-gf-tirra: Tirra reads in a modern, neutral voice, its round forms curving like open parentheses. And paragraphs of it keep that rhythm going, a sans-serif sitting below the lo-fi, retro Silkscreen heading.
gen-silkscreen-gf-titillium-web: Titillium Web is a contemporary, approachable sans with stroke ends set far apart, which gives its text plenty of daylight. Silkscreen on top adds a lo-fi, retro jolt with its single line weight.
gen-silkscreen-gf-tomorrow: Silkscreen draws its bowls at stem thickness, a lo-fi, retro heading with space around every letter. Yet Tomorrow lets its bowls open like a cupped palm of clay, and that clean softness is the strongest thing here.
gen-silkscreen-gf-trispace: Spaghetti lines, lo-fi and retro: Silkscreen leaves space around every letter you can almost feel. But Trispace, a plain sans with sparse, widely set letters, would sprawl if the body were made large.
gen-silkscreen-gf-tsukimi-rounded: Silkscreen is a lo-fi, retro display face with space around every letter you can almost feel. Tsukimi Rounded takes over below with round forms like open parentheses, stroke edges running parallel through every curve.
